decks.label: Tavuista sanoja · talo ja kala
decks.comboAudit: All 64 combinations enumerated and screened for vulgar/anatomy/slur/toilet surfaces (kikkeli/pillu/paska/kusi/kakka class). Structural exclusions: no 'no' card (pano impossible); 'ka' deliberately dropped from column 2 so kaka is NOT formable (kakka-adjacent giggle magnet in a K-1 class) — cost was sika and muka, replaced by 'su' which yields sisu and musu. Flagged sensitive: pana (colloquial vulgar slang; pa+na kept because pa carries palo/pala/papu/pata/pato and na carries kana/muna/juna — the flag suppresses it from chains and celebration). muna kept as a plain real word with its egg badge — standard aapinen vocabulary; the picture anchors the meaning. Colloquial-but-dictionary words musu (kiss) and musa (music) classified real; tasa/taka-type bound stems and names (Jusu, Vapu) left robot. Vowel harmony legal by construction: every card is back-vowel or neutral (a/o/u + i).
decks.notes: KÄTS starter: open CV syllables slide together into 2-syllable words (tavuista sanoiksi). Back-vowel space only; the front-vowel sister deck is fi-etuvokaalit. Real density 23/64.

decks.label: Pitkät tavut · kuk-ka ja pal-lo
decks.comboAudit: All 30 combinations enumerated and screened for vulgar/anatomy/slur/toilet surfaces — the space is clean (kukko, kulli, paska, pillu, kakka not formable: no ko/li/sa cards). Geminates split across the card seam exactly as Finnish tavutus divides them: kuk-ka, pal-lo, ket-tu, lip-pu, suk-ka, tak-ka. Non-matching combos (kuk+lo, suk+pa) yield robot words with non-native clusters — TTS reads them syllabically, which is itself a useful contrast against the geminate hits. palka left robot deliberately: palkka needs kk, and hearing pal+ka fall short of palkka is the whole kesto point.
decks.notes: THE flagship fi deck: kaksoiskonsonantti (geminate) heard as a long sound across the syllable seam — the single most important spelling skill in Finnish alkuopetus. Closed first syllable + open second syllable; all back-vowel/neutral. Real density 7/30.

decks.label: Etuvokaalit · kynä ja pesä
decks.comboAudit: All 49 combinations enumerated and screened for vulgar/anatomy/slur/toilet surfaces — the space is clean (pylly, kyrpä, pillu not formable: no py card, no geminate ll). Vowel harmony legal by construction: every card is front-vowel or neutral (y/ä/ö + e/i), so no combo can violate harmony. Classification calls: pesi (past of pestä) and peli real; sysi (dictionary: charcoal, as in sysimusta) real; kyly (dialectal/Kalevala sauna word) and mäsä (bound colloquial stem) left robot; vesä left robot (the real word is back-vowel vesa). syki left robot — the verb is sykkiä, imperfect sykki.
decks.notes: Front-vowel sister of the starter deck: y, ä, ö with neutral e/i. The 7-word chain vesi→veli→peli→pesi→käsi→käki→mäki is the deck's showpiece — one card flick per step, all real words. Real density 14/49.

decks.label: Äänteistä tavuiksi · k + a = ka
decks.comboAudit: All 80 combinations enumerated and screened — a bare C+V space cannot surface the kusi/paska class (two cards only, no si/ka codas). Expert confirmation: vowel harmony is a word-level constraint in Finnish; ANY consonant + ANY vowel is a fully legal syllable in isolation (kä, ko, py, mö all fine), so no harmony filtering is needed or wanted here. Long-vowel cards aa/uu let the child hear kesto at the äänne level: ka vs kaa, ku vs kuu. Many combos happen to be real words (maa, puu, suu, kuu, luu, syy, työ-adjacent) — by design this deck carries no real map: it drills the slide, not word recognition.
decks.notes: The KÄTS liukuminen drill: slide from the consonant sound into the vowel without stopping — äänteistä tavuiksi. This is the first blending skill in Finnish alkuopetus, before any word-level deck. No badges, no TTS celebration: mouths only.
